details.answer:
Based on the provided document chunks, self-attention layers are faster than recurrent layers in terms of computational complexity when the sequence length n is smaller than the representation dimensionality d. This is because self-attention layers connect all positions with a constant number of sequentially executed operations, whereas recurrent layers require O(n) sequential operations.

Additionally, self-attention layers can be parallelized more easily than recurrent layers, making them faster for tasks involving very long sequences. However, for tasks involving very long sequences, self-attention could be restricted to considering only a neighborhood of the input sequence to improve computational performance.

It's worth noting that the complexity of a separable convolution is equal to the combination of a self-attention layer and a point-wise feed-forward layer, which is the approach taken in the model.
